title: Window Node Moves Across Screen Depending on Window Node Size
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
4.7.2-stable
4.5.1-stable
4.4.1-stable
4.1-stable
4.1-beta1
4.1-dev3
4.1-dev2
It is not reproducible, as far as i could tell, in:
4.1-dev1
4.0.4-stable
4.0-stable
those were the versions i tested.
It seems to be reproduced on both Mobile & Forward+/Computer. Not sure about Compatibility.

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Mobile) - dedicated Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.7088) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12450H (12 threads) - 7.74 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

This bug effects the "Window" node. Not the game window itself, but the Window Node. When you click the bottom panel buttons such as "Output", "Debugger", "Animation", etc. The Window Node's position changes, the place seems to depend on window node's size property. I attempted to put my window node at 1400, 142. It changed to several different positions depending on size. It seems to change y value to 36, or keeps the same. X value seems to change roughly relative to the window size, with a number consistent usually to 1204.
This happens when reloading projects, this happens when pressing the panel buttons, and this also happens when zooming out. This seems to only happen to absolute positioned windows. Centered containers to main window or primary screen seem to not be effected. If the position is a negative position, when u zoom out, click the bottom panel/console buttons, or reload the project, x becomes 0, seemingly. It does not require saving the scene, and bugs quietly with no error, essentially immediately considering that version of the scene present despite the position change. It also shows "Set position" in the console, when it happens.

### Steps to reproduce

Making a Node2D.
Adding a Window node to this Node2D.
Changing the position of the Window node to any random positive numbers, eg. (1182, 415).
Zooming out your screen.
OR
Clicking a bottom panel/console button such as "Output" or "Debugger".
OR
Reloading the Project.
You will notice that the Window node seems to set its own position back to a number relating to either same y, y-36, and/or a new position related to window node size property for x.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - Bug visible in brand new projects
